claim.text: The struck vehicle became a hazard by closing within the ego lane, with hazard onset at 6.1333 s and time-to-collision at onset of 1.9427 s.
Perception took 0.182 s from hazard onset to first detection, below the 0.3 s perception threshold.
The handoff at 6.9207 s left 1.0793 s until impact at 8.0 s, below the 1.5 s human perception-response time.
The CAN brake request at 8.3617 s occurred 0.3617 s after impact at 8.0 s.
Brake actuation took 0.14 s from brake request to pressure reached, below the 0.25 s actuation threshold.
The brake log is complete, so the brake timing evidence is not inconclusive on completeness grounds.
With nominal perception 0.2 s, nominal command 0.05 s and nominal tau 0.15 s, the counterfactual avoided contact with a minimum gap of 7.8713 m.
Lighting was daylight, corroborated by an independent second witness look with the same value.
The primary contributing factor was the late handoff: it left 1.0793 s to impact, below the 1.5 s human perception-response time, while the counterfactual with nominal timings avoided contact.
